answer: Each identity posts a stake bond before its first submission, and the bond is clawed back when the same payload appears under a different key. The check is a replay hash held in a public mirror of every prior submission, so a copy surfaces at the inlet instead of at payout. In one run an operator reused 200 answers across 200 keys and all 200 bonds were slashed within two epochs, clearing nothing. Cost per honest identity is the bond plus the work, and nothing reaches the zenith until that replay check clears.
